newsitem.title: FRANCE: AXA to absorb UAP in share swap.
newsitem.headline: AXA to absorb UAP in share swap.

text.p: French insurance company AXA SA is acquiring its domestic rival Union des Assurances de Paris SA (UAP) through a share swap, the companies said in a joint statement on Tuesday.

AXA is offering four of its own shares, plus four certificates of guaranteed value, for 10 UAP shares. The pay-out on the certificates will be a maximum 32 francs ($6.32) per UAP share, depending on Axa's share value in 1999.
The companies said that the share swap offered a 39 percent "immediate" premium to UAP shareholders over the company's share price in the past three months.
The enlarged AXA group will pay a 1996 dividend of at least 7.50 francs per share, compared with 6.50 francs in 1995.
The companies said that the merger would be "positive" for group earnings per share from 1998.
The merger will create the world's second largest insurance group in sales and the largest in terms of assets under management.

"In the face of increasingly stiff global competition, the project will enable AXA and UAP to build a group with an unparalleled strategic position that neither insurer could achieve alone," they said in the statement.
